title: RFID Supplier for Dubai & the UAE — Factory-Direct China
summary: Proud Tek ships RFID to the UAE factory-direct from Shenzhen with Emirates-market spec sheets. The one fact that decides a UHF order: the UAE follows the European allocation, not the US or Australian one — UHF RFID runs at 865-868 MHz (2 W e.r.p.) with an optional 915-921 MHz upper band (4 W e.r.p.) under the TDRA per ETSI EN 302 208, so EU-standard 865-868 MHz inlays are band-correct here and US 902-928 MHz stock is not the default. Access and hotel cards run at 13.56 MHz (HF), which is global. Express air reaches Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah in 3-5 business days; RFID smart cards (HS 8523.52) clear at the 5% GCC customs duty plus 5% VAT, and DDP is available.

sections.title: Get the band right: 865-868 MHz (and the 915-921 MHz upper band) under the TDRA
sections.intro: The single most expensive mistake in cross-border RFID sourcing is band mismatch — and the UAE has a pleasant twist. Unlike Australia or the US (902-928 MHz), the UAE follows the European allocation under the TDRA per ETSI EN 302 208: a primary 865-868 MHz band at 2 W e.r.p., plus an optional 915-921 MHz upper band at 4 W e.r.p. That means an EU-standard 865-868 MHz inlay is already band-correct for the UAE; a US 902-928 MHz-tuned inlay is not the default. New to frequency planning? Start with our [LF vs HF vs UHF guide](/blog/rfid-frequencies-lf-hf-uhf-explained/). (Access cards at 13.56 MHz are global and unaffected.)

sections.title: Landed cost: HS 8523.52, the 5% GCC tariff and 5% VAT
sections.intro: The unit price is the headline; the landed cost is the story. For the UAE there are three characters — the HS line, the GCC common tariff, and VAT. Our [air vs sea freight guide](/blog/rfid-shipping-air-vs-sea-freight-cost-tradeoff/) shows the freight-mode math; the short version is below.

dataHighlight.heading: RFID smart cards enter the UAE at the 5% GCC tariff plus 5% VAT
dataHighlight.text: RFID cards, inlays and tags classify under HS 8523.52 ("smart cards"). The UAE applies the GCC Common Customs Tariff — a 5% duty on the CIF value for most goods — and there is no China-UAE free-trade preference to zero it out, so budget the 5% unless your customs broker confirms an exemption. On top of that, 5% UAE VAT is charged on the customs value (goods + freight + insurance + duty) and is generally recoverable for a VAT-registered importer. Goods held in a Dubai free zone (Jebel Ali, Dubai South) are duty-suspended until they enter the UAE mainland. On a DDP quote, freight, duty, VAT and clearance are all in the price you see.
dataHighlight.source: UAE Federal Tax Authority (VAT 5%); GCC Common Customs Tariff (US Commercial Service — UAE Import Tariffs)

faq.question: Which UHF band do your tags use for the UAE?
faq.answer: The UAE follows the European allocation under the TDRA per ETSI EN 302 208: a primary 865-868 MHz band at 2 W e.r.p. and an optional 915-921 MHz upper band at 4 W e.r.p. We tune passive inlays for 865-868 MHz, so EU-standard 865-868 MHz stock is band-correct here — a US 902-928 MHz-tuned inlay is not the default. HF hotel and access cards at 13.56 MHz are globally harmonised and unaffected; specify 865-868 MHz only for UHF inlay and label orders.

faq.question: Do passive RFID tags need their own TDRA type approval?
faq.answer: No. The regulated radio is the reader/interrogator, which needs TDRA type approval and operates under the Short Range Device class authorization. Passive UHF tags are not transmitters — they backscatter the reader's signal — so what matters is that the tag antenna is tuned for the UAE 865-868 MHz band. When evaluating suppliers, ask for the reader's TDRA approval and the tag's tuning and read data rather than an approval for the tag itself.

faq.question: How do UAE customs duty and VAT work on an order?
faq.answer: RFID smart cards classify under HS 8523.52. The UAE applies the GCC Common Customs Tariff — a 5% duty on the CIF value for most goods, with no China-UAE free-trade preference — plus 5% UAE VAT on the customs value, which is generally recoverable for a VAT-registered importer. Goods held in a Dubai free zone (Jebel Ali, Dubai South) are duty-suspended until they enter the mainland. On a DDP quote, freight, duty, VAT and clearance are included up front — confirm the exact classification and any exemption with your customs broker.

faq.question: How long does shipping from Proud Tek to Dubai take?
faq.answer: Express air freight from Shenzhen to Dubai takes 3-5 business days. Combined with our standard production lead time of 5-7 days, most orders arrive in the UAE within about 10-12 business days of order confirmation. Sea freight into Jebel Ali is available for large-volume orders at lower cost and longer transit.

Because configurations vary, we ship free sample cards to your UAE address so you can confirm compatibility on your live readers before any bulk order.
